outcome: Dilation and evacuation (D&E) complications (cervical laceration, hemorrhage, uterine atony, anesthesia complications, uterine perforation, disseminated intravascular coagulation, and retained products of conception)
Major complications requiring hospitalization, transfusion, or further surgical intervention
cohort: Women who underwent D&E abortion from February 2009 to April 2013 at a hospital-based abortion practice in California.
finding: No association was found between obesity and D&E complications.
